why:
All conversions use the offsets stated in e3: New York UTC-05:00, Tokyo UTC+09:00, Singapore UTC+08:00.
STEP 1. Malik sends the request for a corrected certificate at 3:40 PM Eastern Monday 16 November (e5) = 20:40 UTC Monday 16 November.
STEP 2. Tamesada's flight departs Osaka at 10:10 PM Japan time Monday 16 November = 13:10 UTC Monday 16 November, and lands in Singapore at 4:30 AM Singapore time Tuesday 17 November = 20:30 UTC Monday 16 November (e7). She is unreachable for that entire interval. Note the ordering that matters: the request arrives at 20:40 UTC, ten minutes AFTER she is already on the ground -- it is sitting in her inbox when she next looks, not lost in the air.
STEP 3. She clears her compliance inbox from the arrivals hall between 45 and 60 minutes after landing (e8), i.e. between 21:15 and 21:30 UTC Monday 16 November, and reads the request then.
STEP 4. Issuing the corrected certificate takes her 20 minutes and needs nobody else (e6, e9), so she sends it between 21:35 and 21:50 UTC. Delivery adds at most 2 minutes (e10), so it lands in Malik's inbox between 21:37 and 21:52 UTC Monday 16 November = between 4:37 PM and 4:52 PM Eastern Monday 16 November.
STEP 5. Malik's last email check on Monday is 4:30 PM Eastern, and he reads mail at no other time (e11). Under every value in the 45-to-60-minute range of e8 the certificate arrives after 4:30 PM, so he does not see it on Monday.
STEP 6. He is absent for all of Tuesday 17 November and touches neither email nor the filing system, and no colleague may act for him (e12). Nothing moves on Tuesday.
STEP 7. He returns on Wednesday 18 November. His first check is 8:00 AM Eastern (e11), at which he sees the corrected certificate. With it, the document set is complete (e4, e14).
STEP 8. Preparing and submitting the entry takes 45 minutes (e13), so the entry is submitted at 8:45 AM Eastern on Wednesday 18 November. The system accepts and acknowledges filings at that hour and was operating normally (e13). The deadline is 9:00 AM Eastern that day.
ANSWER: yes, by 15 minutes. The uncertainty declared in e8 does not need resolving by convenience: at both ends of the 45-to-60-minute range Malik still misses Monday's 4:30 PM check and still first sees the certificate at 8:00 AM Wednesday, so the outcome is identical across the whole declared range.
WHERE A CARELESS SYSTEM GOES WRONG. Treating Tamesada as unavailable until she is next at her Osaka desk, or mishandling the date-line arithmetic so that her 4:30 AM Tuesday Singapore landing is placed after rather than before Malik's Monday-afternoon email, makes the corrected certificate arrive too late and yields 'no'.
